target_constraint: Must prevent bacterial colonization at implant-abutment interface
observed_phenomenon: Peri-implantitis causing bone loss and implant failure
mechanism: Multifunctional implant surface chemistry and micro/nanoscale topography can simultaneously regulate microbial colonization, immune responses, and tissue integration, thereby preventing biofilm-associated infection and promoting osseointegration.
intervention: Apply a bi-layered nano-fluorapatite/nano-chitosan (nFA/nCS) coating to the implant-abutment interface of a dental implant, replacing the standard platform switching design. The nFA layer promotes osseointegration while the nCS layer provides antimicrobial activity, creating a dual-function barrier that prevents bacterial colonization at the interface and supports bone regeneration.
expected_effect: Reduced bacterial adhesion and biofilm formation at the implant-abutment interface, leading to decreased incidence of peri-implantitis, reduced bone loss, and improved long-term implant survival compared to platform switching alone.
falsification_test: In an in vitro biofilm assay using a multispecies oral biofilm model, compare bacterial colony-forming units (CFUs) on nFA/nCS-coated implant-abutment assemblies versus uncoated platform-switching assemblies after 7 days. If the coated assemblies do not show a statistically significant reduction in CFUs (p<0.05), the intervention fails to prevent bacterial colonization.
